full_prd_text:
## Problem Statement
The TransferSaga in payment-platform occasionally double-reverses the wallet ledger when Payliance pushes a return mid-saga. Wallet ledger correctness depends on saga + walletapi cooperation.

## Solution
Refactor the saga's return-handling path to be idempotent on (transferId, returnReasonCode); introduce a deduplicated walletapi ledger-reversal entry point.

## User Stories
1. As payment-platform, I want to deduplicate inbound ACH returns by (transferId, returnReasonCode), so that the saga reverses the ledger exactly once.
2. As the TransferSaga, I want to emit ReturnReceived as a first-class event, so that downstream listeners subscribe to a single transition.
3. As walletapi, I want to reject duplicate ledger-reversal calls at the API boundary, so that double-reversals are caught even if the saga retries.

## Cross-Application Impact
- payment-platform: refactor TransferSaga return-handler chain into an explicit ReturnReceived aggregate event, add idempotency guard at the SQS consumer.
- walletapi: add deduplicated ledger-reversal entry point keyed on (transferId, returnReasonCode); reject duplicates at the API boundary.

## Implementation Decisions
- New aggregate event ReturnReceived(transferId, returnReasonCode, providerReference) flows from SqsConsumer to TransferSaga.
- TransferSaga calls WalletLedgerClient with the dedup key; WalletLedgerClient enforces a unique index on (transferId, returnReasonCode).
- Spike: confirm SQS retry semantics for duplicate-suppression at the consumer boundary.
- Metrics: saga.return.deduped, saga.return.received.

## Out of Scope
- Payliance contract changes
- Replacing SQS with EventBridge
- Customer-facing rebrand

## Further Notes
Stage rollout behind transfer-saga-v3 Split.io flag.
